content.introduction: This week's economic data highlights include the October employment report on Friday, which is expected to show a stronger payroll gain than the consensus, approximately 55,000, according to Yardeni. The sources also mention manufacturing and services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) survey results from S&P and the Institute of Supply Management (ISM). Additionally, earnings reports from major companies like Apple and Qualcomm are anticipated, with 31% of the S&P 500 companies set to report. The Bank of England is expected to raise its rate by 25bps to 4.00%.
body:
We'll also get manufacturing and services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) survey results from S&P and the Institute of Supply Management (ISM).

Note, too, that we'll hear from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who, along with Fed Governor Lisa Cook, dissented from the decision to hold interest rates at the October Fed meeting, on Thursday morning.

## From just ~~$107.88~~ $24.99 for Kiplinger Personal Finance [...] Friday, November 6: Nonfarm payrolls report: It may have been a cooler-than-expected September jobs report. But, focused on the inflation problem, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sees no signs of instability in the workforce or the unemployment rate.

Read on to see the entire weekly economic calendar of the most important upcoming economic reports scheduled to be released in the next several days. At times, we provide expanded previews and recaps for select reports. [...] "We estimate that nonfarm payroll employment grew 50,000 in October, following gains in August (+133,000) and September (+29,000)," writes Barclays Chief U.S. Economist Marc Giannoni in a preview of incoming Jobs Friday data.

According to Giannoni's math, his headline forecast would work out to a three-month moving average of 71,000 new jobs, ahead of the 28,000 pace for the three months through July.

(3) Earnings. The earnings reporting season continues this week, with 31% of the S&P 500 companies set to report. Apple, Palantir, AMD, Arista Networks, Qualcomm, and Arm headline the list.

Analysts’ consensus estimates imply Q3-2026 operating EPS growth for S&P 500 companies of 23.8% y/y, down slightly from 24.1% last week, after Alphabet, Amazon, and Intel missed estimates (chart). Q4 growth estimates held at 30.2%. [...] (1) Employment. October’s employment report is the economic headliner. Payrolls rose 29,000 in September, lowering the three-month average to 50,700 (chart). The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, while average hourly earnings increased just 0.1% m/m. We expect a stronger payroll gain than the consensus, of approximately 55,000. [...] The Bank of England (Thu) looks set to raise its rate by 25bps to 4.00%, with 98% odds priced into the markets. The markets see a 35% chance of another hike in December.

The Eurozone’s flash CPI (Wed) is expected to rise in October from September’s 3.8% y/y, with the core rate holding at 2.5%. Among the major economies, Spain’s headline rate was the highest at 5.0% in September and Germany’s the lowest at 3.3% (chart).
